samples.text:
The maps shows how a university campus changed between 2010 and 2025. Overall, many new buildings were added, and the campus become more crowded.

In 2010, there was a main teaching building in the centre and a entrance road coming from the south. There was a lake in the north-east, student halls in the north-west and a library in the west. In the south there were a big car park and a sports field, and there were many trees in the north.

In 2025, the teaching building, the lake and the old student halls are still there. However, the car park in the south-west was replaced by a science and engineering building, and a smaller car park was built next to it. The sports field is also changed, there is a sports centre and a pitch now. The trees in the north was cut down and new student halls were built there. Also, the library was extended to the east and west. Finally, a cycle path was added which goes across the campus from west to east, and a café was built in the east near to the lake.
samples.why: Basic overview · key changes covered in a before-then-after listing · simple linking (Also, Finally) · adequate vocabulary · several errors in agreement, articles, tense and a comma splice, none blocking meaning.

samples.text:
The maps illustrate the development of a university campus over a fifteen-year period from 2010 to 2025. Overall, the campus has been significantly expanded with new academic, residential and sports buildings, largely at the expense of parking space and green areas, although its central core has remained the same.

The main teaching building, the entrance road leading to it from the south, the lake in the north-east and the original student halls in the north-west were all unaffected. The library in the west, however, has been extended on both sides, and the trees which covered the north of the campus have been cleared to make way for new student halls.

The southern part of the campus has seen the greatest change. The large car park in the south-west has been replaced by a science and engineering building, with only a much smaller car park beside it, next to the entrance road. To the south-east, the sports field has been divided into a sports centre and a pitch. In addition, a cycle path now crosses the whole campus from west to east, just south of the teaching building, and a small café have opened on the eastern edge, south of the lake.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying expansion and what was lost · logical grouping by area · good range of cohesive devices · appropriate less common vocabulary · mostly error-free with a minor agreement slip.

samples.text:
The two plans show how a university campus was redeveloped between 2010 and 2025. What stands out is the considerable expansion of buildings, particularly in the south and north of the site, which came at the cost of most of the car parking and all of the woodland, while the central teaching building and the lake were left untouched.

In the north, the cluster of trees that once separated the original student halls from the lake has been cleared, and a second block of student halls has been constructed in its place. The library on the western side, meanwhile, has been enlarged in both directions.

The southern half of the campus has been transformed most radically. The extensive car park in the south-west has been largely taken over by a new science and engineering building, leaving a compact car park squeezed between this building and the main entrance road. On the opposite side of the road, the sports field has been partly built on, with an indoor sports centre now standing beside a smaller outdoor pitch. Finally, a cycle path has been laid across the campus, just south of the teaching building, and a café has been added on the eastern boundary.
samples.why: Skilful overview highlighting gains and losses · features precisely located and compared · cohesion managed effortlessly · wide, accurate vocabulary (redeveloped, taken over, compact) · varied complex structures with no noticeable errors.
